title: Pairs and odd ones out
_map: Lesson map: Pairs and odd ones out (Y2). Big idea: even numbers split into pairs; odd numbers always leave one over.
_stepChain: counting → pairs of sheep → some numbers make only pairs → some leave one over → named even and odd → test odd + odd with animals → make a rule

talk.ask: What's the difference between an even number and an odd number?
talk.goodAnswer: even numbers make pairs with none left over; odd numbers always have one left over.

talk.ask: Is odd + odd odd or even? Why?
talk.goodAnswer: even: each odd number has one left over, and the two left-over ones make a new pair.

handsOn: Grab a handful of Lego bricks and pair them up. Is your number odd or even? Then grab another handful, put them together, and check again.

narration.text: The sheep are going for a walk, and they like to walk in pairs: two together, side by side.
Choose how many sheep go for a walk, then tap the hammer. Do they all get a partner? Try lots of numbers.
Some numbers make pairs with nobody left out: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Numbers like those are called even.
Other numbers always leave one sheep without a partner: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Numbers like those are called odd.
Here's an experiment. 3 sheep join 5 sheep. 3 is odd, and 5 is odd.

question.prompt: Will 3 and 5 together be odd or even? Make a guess.
question.reveal: Even! 3 and 5 make 8. Each odd number had one sheep left over, and the two left-over sheep became a new pair.

rule.text: Even makes pairs. Odd has one left over.
rule.ask: Can you say what makes a number odd? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Even numbers make pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always have one left over.

bonus.reveal: Odd. 100 makes 50 pairs, and 1 more is left over.
